title: Achieving Wide-Temperature-Range Physical and Chemical Hydrogen Sorption in a Structural Optimized Mg/N-Doped Porous Carbon Nanocomposite
material_description: rN-pC | N-doped porous carbon: ZIF-8 nanoparticles pyrolysed at 1000 °C for 30 min under Ar/5% H2 (N-pC), then treated in NH3 at 750 °C for 30 min; hierarchical micro/mesoporous, N 5.97 at% (XPS)
activation_method: NH3 treatment at 750 °C for 30 min after pyrolysis (NH3 etching and N enrichment)
functional_groups: pyridinic N, pyrrolic N, graphitic N, quaternary N, oxidized N (-NO2); C-N/C-O, C=O (XPS)
source_location: main p.8, Fig. 2a, series '-196 °C' (open squares), marker 01 of 32 (ordered by pressure)
notes: archive: fig2a_rNpC_77K_excess_m01.json; digitized pressure 0.004590 MPa (x10 = bar); digitized uptake -0.00256 wt% (negative, origin marker) set to 0; T printed -196 °C (+273.15 = 77.15 K); fitted Toth curve and absolute curve not used for this point
basis_evidence: Main p.7: "The H2 storage performance of rN-pC are evaluated through high-pressure (0–6 MPa) excess H2 adsorption at –196 and –186 °C (Fig. 2a). These are modeled using a semi-empirical methodology (Eq. S1), then converted to absolute H2 uptake." Fig. 2a reports the excess isotherms (markers) and the "absolute adsorption" curves side by side; p.7: "An absolute gravimetric H2 uptake ~3.4 and ~3.0 wt% is recorded ..."
measuring_lab_id: Li group, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
